# Flux 3 Image Lands in Picsart: 4K Output and 10 Reference Images

> **In short:** Black Forest Labs' new image model, Flux 3 Image, is now available inside Picsart's AI Playground, with native 2K and 4K output and room for up to 10 reference images. It's built for ads, posters, and brand assets — and it can edit existing images too.

If you've ever tried to whip up a quick poster, social ad, or product mock-up and ended up with a fuzzy picture that fell apart the moment you zoomed in, you already understand why a model promising **full-resolution output** (high enough pixel count to look sharp on a poster, not just a phone screen) is real news. Picsart just added one.

## What is Flux 3 Image?

Flux 3 Image is the newest **image model** (an AI trained to generate pictures from a text prompt or uploaded reference) from Black Forest Labs, a research group known for its open work in image generation. Think of it as the engine under the hood: you describe a scene or drop in references, and the model paints the result.

According to Black Forest Labs, the focus this time is on three things — cleaner **layout control** (deciding where things sit in the frame), more **precise edits** (changing just the part you want without redrawing everything), and higher native resolution.

## What's new in Picsart's AI Playground

Picsart — a photo and design app popular with creators and small businesses — has put Flux 3 Image inside its **AI Playground**, a hub where users can try different image models side by side.

Here's what stands out from the announcement:

- **Native 2K and 4K output.** The model generates images at high resolution by default, so what you download is sharp enough for print, not just a screen.
- **Up to 10 reference images.** Most image models accept one or two visual guides. Flux 3 Image, Picsart says, lets you feed in up to 10 — handy for keeping a character's face, a product, or a brand color consistent across a set of pictures.
- **Layout control and precise edits.** You can describe the scene in detail, drop in references, and then edit the result. Picsart frames this as output ready for ads, posters, and brand assets — closer to a finished file than a rough draft.

The same model also edits existing images, so you can change a small part of a picture without redrawing the whole thing.

## What this means for you

- **If you're a casual creator:** A high-resolution output means your blog header, event poster, or Instagram post won't pixelate when someone zooms in. Multiple reference images mean you can finally keep your cat looking like the same cat across ten drawings.
- **If you run a small business or work in marketing:** This is closer to a finished asset than a rough sketch. Picsart's framing — ads, posters, brand work — points to the moment between "idea" and "publish," where a lot of time usually goes to resizing and re-cutting.
- **If you're just curious:** AI Playground lets you test different models in one place. Trying Flux 3 Image against other image models in the same interface is the fastest way to feel out what each one does well.
- **If you already use Picsart:** The next time you open AI Playground, look for Flux 3 Image in the model list. If you produce brand assets in batches, the 10-reference-image limit is the feature worth testing first — that's how you keep a character or product consistent across a whole series.

## Wrap-up

Flux 3 Image joins a crowded field of image models, but Picsart's pitch is concrete: bigger files, more references, and edits that don't destroy the original picture. The best way to know if it works for you is to open Picsart, pick the model, and try a prompt you actually care about — a poster for an event, a product shot, a portrait with a specific look. Five minutes of testing will tell you more than any announcement.
